name: New Mexico

sales.rateNote: New Mexico has a gross receipts tax (GRT), not a sales tax: it is imposed on the seller, who commonly passes it on to the buyer as a separately stated charge. 4.875% is the state portion; counties and municipalities add local option increments.

local.levies: county and municipal local option gross receipts tax increments (set by county commissions and municipal councils), collected by the state and distributed back
local.capNote: Since July 1, 2025, local rate changes take effect only in July (January only in special situations such as a natural disaster).

groceries.note: Retail food stores certified under the federal SNAP definition deduct qualifying food sales from gross receipts (Section 7-9-92); alcohol, tobacco and hot prepared food for immediate consumption are not deductible.

clothing.note: Clothing is subject to GRT except during the annual back-to-school holiday (items under $100).

otherRates.item: Leased vehicle gross receipts tax (short-term passenger car rentals)
otherRates.note: Imposed in addition to GRT on qualifying short-term leases of passenger cars from fleets of five or more, plus a $2-per-day leased vehicle surcharge.
Sales of vehicles subject to the motor vehicle excise tax are exempt from GRT (Section 7-9-22); the excise tax is administered separately.

holidays2026.name: Back-to-school gross receipts tax holiday
holidays2026.items: clothing and shoes under $100; computers and e-readers up to $1,000 and related peripherals up to $500; school supplies under $30 (book bags, backpacks, maps, globes under $100; calculators under $200)

sales.holidayNote: Statutory holiday (Section 7-9-95): from 12:01 a.m. on the last Friday in July to midnight the following Sunday; 2026 dates derived from that rule.

useTax.note: Compensating tax at the state rate of 4.875% plus any local option, due on property or services bought without GRT and used in New Mexico.

facts.text: The state GRT rate went from 5.0% (January–June 2023) to 4.875% on July 1, 2023, and the July 2026–June 2027 rate schedule keeps it at 4.875%.
GRT also applies to most services, not just goods; there is no deduction for a business's own expenses.
Remote sellers and marketplace providers owe GRT once they have $100,000 of taxable New Mexico receipts in the previous calendar year.
If the business passes GRT on to the customer, it must be separately stated on the invoice.
Feminine hygiene products have been deductible from GRT since July 1, 2022 (Section 7-9-120).
Rate changes effective July 1, 2026 raised local GRT in locations including Los Ranchos de Albuquerque and much of Colfax County (Raton, Angel Fire, Cimarron and others).

property.levied: Local: county assessors value property and county treasurers bill and collect taxes for counties, municipalities, school districts and other districts; the state Taxation and Revenue Department's Property Tax Division oversees assessors and values certain state-assessed property.

assessment.text: Property is valued at current and correct value as of January 1; the New Mexico Constitution caps the taxable share at 33 1/3% of value. Residential valuation increases are limited to the higher of 3% over the prior year or 6.1% over two years (Section 7-36-21.2), except for new construction and improvements.
assessment.capText: Property is valued at current and correct value as of January 1; the New Mexico Constitution caps the taxable share at 33 1/3% of value. Residential valuation increases are limited to the higher of 3% over the prior year or 6.1% over two years (Section 7-36-21.2), except for new construction and improvements.

homestead.name: Homeowner exemptions
homestead.text: TRD states that exemptions are available for qualifying homeowners; they reduce full value to the net taxable value shown on the county assessor's Notice of Valuation, which is the basis of the county treasurer's bill.

otherRelief.name: Valuation freeze for low-income owners 65+ or disabled
otherRelief.text: Single-family homes owned and occupied by people 65+ or disabled with modified gross income up to $42,900 (tax year 2025 order) have their value limited (Section 7-36-21.3).

otherRelief.name: Veteran exemption
otherRelief.text: Up to $10,000 of taxable value is exempt for New Mexico resident veterans or their unmarried surviving spouses; 100% service-connected disabled veterans' principal residence can be fully exempt.

otherRelief.name: Low-income property tax rebate (county option)
otherRelief.text: Counties may adopt a rebate for residents with modified gross income up to $24,000, claimed on the state income tax return (PIT-RC); currently Los Alamos, Santa Fe and Doña Ana counties.

facts.text: County assessors mail Notices of Valuation around April 1; protests are due 30 days after the notice is mailed and are heard by a County Valuation Protests Board that includes a state Property Tax Division appraiser.
Owners must report certain changes in their property's value to the assessor by the last day of February each year (Section 7-38-8).
The 3%-a-year residential cap does not apply in the first year a property is valued or to physical improvements (except solar installations).
Delinquent property taxes are collected by the state Property Tax Division, which offers installment agreements and ultimately auctions properties.
